The (Better) Case For European Banks

Tan Kai Xian, Cedric Gemehl

Gavekal Research | 10 Aug 2026

After more than a decade in the wilderness, European bank stocks have now had four good years, outperforming their US counterparts since 2022 in US dollar terms. The question is whether this outperformance can continue. The short answer is yes. European bank stocks are no longer priced at distressed levels. But with the earnings outlooks for European and US banks both solid, there is still room for European valuations to improve compared with the US.The relative performance of European bank stocks began to pick up in 2022. The initial driver was an acceleration in earnings and returns on equity compared with the US bank sector as Europe emerged from the deflationary overhang of the 2010s, with nominal growth and interest rates both rising (see Neither US Exceptionalism Nor A European Boom: Macro Edition). But the wilderness years cast a long shadow. Expectations that European banks would remain a value trap meant that over 2022-23 the sector continued to derate both against its own historical record and relative to US banks (see the chart below and US Exceptionalism Versus European Pessimism).
